To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GOS degradation was higher in the pig TIM-2 model, whereas L. amylovorus DSM16698 was more resistant to the colonic microbiota in human TIM-2 model; the growth of L. amylovoruss DSM16698 was stimulated by GOS, and co-administration with Bb-12 increased lactate accumulation in human TIM- 2 model.
the presence of GOS in the TIM-2 system increased the growth of lacto- and bifidobacterial populations and stimulated the production of metabolites, such as short chain fatty acids.

the impact of potentially pre- and probiotics (L. amyolvorus DSM 1668, GOS and B. animalis Bb12) on GOS fermentation, microbial community structure and metabolite production differed between the TIM-2 model set up with pig faecas and with human faecas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of in vitro systems that mimic the human large intestine and are suitable for the study of probiotic/prebiotic intervention.
the development and validation of a novel, dynamic and reproducible in vitro model for studying the effects of pre- and probiotics on the human gut microbiota.
the development of an in vitro model to evaluate the impact that pre- and probiotics have on the human gut microbiota.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of GOS and Bifid. animalis ssp lactis Bb12 on growth of potentially probiotic strain L. amylovorus DSM16698 and metabolites production were similar in the TIM-2 set up with human and pig faecal material.
L. amylovorus DSM16698 has a probiotic potential and that GOS can be used as prebiotics for both pig and human microbiota.

the effects of GOS, L. amylovorus and Bb- 12 on microbial growth and metabolite production are highly dependent on the microbial community composition, which in turn is influenced by the host organism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of pre- and probiotics has a positive impact on the growth of lacto- and bifidobacterial species in the colon and on the production of lactate, which is a potential source of energy for the host.

L. amylovorus DSM16698 is a promising probiotic strain, as it is capable of surviving in the colon and of stimulating the growth of other probiotic strains and lactobacilli in the presence of the prebiotic GOS.
L. amylovorus was not able to survive in the presence of GOS, but the presence of G. Bb-12 was able to stimulate the growth of L. amylovorous.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a validated in vitro model can be a useful tool in pre-screening of pre- and probiotics for their potential to affect the human gut.

the TIM-2 model is suitable for studying the impact of prebiotics and probiotics on microbial growth, metabolite production and microbial community dynamics in a human or pig model of the large intestinal tract.
the TIM-2 is a valuable tool to evaluate the effect of probiotic strains on microbial community structure, metabolite production, and prebiotic degradation in vitro.
